tickets.summary: App scaffold: one-file build, test runner, empty page
tickets.why:
Every other WarpView ticket writes a module under app/src and needs one way to test it and one way to turn the
    modules into the single viewer file. Without a fixed build, folder layout and test command, sixteen agents invent
    sixteen conventions, imports break across modules, and the release cannot produce a file that opens from disk
    with no server and no network.
tickets.what:
1. `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/package.json`: `"type": "module"`, scripts `test` = `node --test`, `build` = `node build.mjs`
    (writes `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/dist/viewer.html`), `release` = `node build.mjs --release` (writes `WARPDEMO/WarpView/viewer.html`);
    devDependencies pinned exactly: `esbuild` 0.24.0 and `jsdom` 25.0.1. 2. `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/build.mjs`: bundle `src/main.mjs`
    with esbuild (format iife, target es2020, no minify), inline the bundle and every `src/**/*.css` (files under
    `src/styles/` first, then path order) into `src/shell.html`, and print `viewer: <path> <bytes>`. 3. `src/shell.html`:
    the regions of SPEC §10.1 with their ids and the data slot `<script id="warp-data" type="application/json">null</script>`.
    4. `src/main.mjs`: export `createApp({root, plugins})`; for now it renders the empty state of SPEC §10.9.
    5. `src/core/util.mjs`: the helpers of SPEC §4.6 (esc, num, fmtH, fmtN, pct, parseTime, ago, stamp, natKey,
    natCmp, hashHue) with tests beside them. 6. `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/.gitignore`: `node_modules/` and `dist/`. 7. `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/test/dom.mjs`:
    a helper that loads a built HTML file in jsdom with a given fixture placed in the data slot.
outOfScope: Any screen beyond the empty state

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a clean checkout, when `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app ci && npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app run build` runs, then `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/dist/viewer.html` exists, has exactly one inline <script> without src, no <link rel=stylesheet>, and shows the text 'Open a Warp run' when opened.
Given util.mjs, when called, then fmtH(null) is '—', fmtH(7) is '7h', fmtH(105.5) is '106h', fmtH(36.24) is '36.2h', natCmp('WV-2','WV-10') < 0 and esc('<a href="x">') is '<a href="x">'.
Given the built file, when searched for 'http://' and 'https://', then neither appears outside string literals that the spec allows (none in the scaffold): the page fetches nothing.
Given a CSS file that fails to parse or a missing src/main.mjs, when build runs, then it exits with status 1 and prints the file name; no partial viewer.html is left behind.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then the util and build tests pass.

nfrs.text: No network calls: the built file loads nothing from outside itself.

tickets.summary: Theme tokens, layout styles, dark mode, phone width and print
tickets.why:
The viewer must look like the reference page in both themes, at phone width and on paper. If each view
    picks its own colors and spacing, the six status colors drift, dark mode loses contrast, the page scrolls
    sideways on a phone and printing cuts the swimlane. One owned set of tokens and layout rules keeps every
    view consistent and lets the view tickets run in parallel without touching shared CSS.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/styles/tokens.css` and `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/styles/layout.css` from SPEC §12 and the reference page
    `WARPDEMO/WarpView/ui/reference/warp-dashboard.html`. 1. Tokens on `:root` exactly as SPEC §12.1: surface, ink, line and brand
    colors and the six status colors `--c-done --c-err --c-prog --c-rev --c-qa --c-todo`, plus `--tint` and `--tint-todo`.
    2. Dark values under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and again
    under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. 3. Layout for the top bar, chips, buttons, menu, headline, tabs, metric cards,
    stack bars, legend chips, search, segmented controls, panels, toasts, drop overlay, empty state (SPEC §10).
    4. `@media (max-width: 640px)` rules of SPEC §10.11 (16 px gutter, cards in one column, top bar wraps).
    5. `@media print` rules of SPEC §10.12 (light tokens, controls hidden, exact colors).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given tokens.css, when parsed, then every custom property listed in SPEC §12.1 is defined on :root with the listed light value and redefined in both dark blocks with the listed dark value.

Given the built page with `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json`, when rendered at 1600 px, then cards, chips and panels match `WARPDEMO/WarpView/ui/screens/swimlane-plan.png` in order, spacing and color (same tokens, no new colors).
Given a 390 px wide viewport, when the page renders, then document.documentElement.scrollWidth equals the viewport width (no sideways scroll) and metric cards are in one column.
Given any CSS file in src/, when searched, then no color literal for a status appears outside tokens.css (views use var(--c-*) only).
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then the tokens test (parses tokens.css and compares to SPEC §12.1) passes.

tickets.summary: Status model: sixteen Warp statuses on six colors
tickets.why:
Warp has sixteen ticket statuses and the screens show six categories. If the mapping lives in each view,
    the swimlane, board, table, legend and totals disagree about what is in progress, and a status Warp adds later
    silently becomes invisible. One module owns the mapping, the aliases for hand-written files and the
    ticket state.json states, and the rule for unknown values.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/core/status.mjs` per SPEC §5. Export: 1. `CATS` — the six categories in display order
    with keys `done err prog rev qa todo` and labels Completed, Errored / Parked, In Progress, In Review, QA Ready,
    To Do. 2. `STATUS_CAT` — the sixteen Warp statuses of SPEC §5.1 to a category key. 3. `STATUS_ALIAS` for labels
    found in hand-written files (in_progress, qa_ready, to_do, completed, errored, failed, bugbot and the others in
    §5.2). 4. `STATE_STATUS` — ticket state.json states to beam statuses (§5.3). 5. `TERMINAL`, `ACTIVE`,
    `normStatus(raw)` (lower-case, spaces and hyphens to underscores, alias, empty to queued), `catOf(status)`
    (unknown to todo), `bucketOf(cat)` (rev and qa count as prog in totals), `catColor(cat)` returning the CSS
    variable, and `statusText(status)`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given each of the sixteen statuses in SPEC §5.1, when catOf runs, then it returns the category listed there; merged, done and skipped are 'done'; awaiting_approval is 'qa'; alarm, parked and blocked are 'err'.
Given 'In Progress', 'QA-Ready' and 'to do', when normStatus runs, then it returns coding, awaiting_approval and queued.
Given an empty string, null or 'teleporting', when normStatus and catOf run, then empty and null become queued and 'teleporting' stays as is with category todo.
Given STATE_STATUS, when asked for 'heartbeat' or 'done', then it returns undefined: those states never move a ticket.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then status.test.mjs passes and checks every key in `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/categories.json`.

tickets.summary: Read beam, status, ticket state and export files into runs
tickets.why:
The viewer is only as good as what it reads. Warp writes a beam, a status file, one state file per ticket,
    a plan export and, for named runs, a mirror per run. File names change between Warp versions, so the reader must
    classify by content, merge the copies of one run, and let a newer ticket state move an open ticket. Getting this
    wrong shows stale or doubled tickets and wrong totals.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/load/parse/parse.mjs` per SPEC §3 and §4. 1. `classify(data)` returns beam, status, ticket
    or null by content (§3.1). 2. `runFromBeam(doc)` builds the Run model of §4 from a beam or a `kind: warp-plan`
    export (estimate at top level, exportedAt), including gate greenAt, evidence, checks and if-red. 3. `runFromStatus`
    for status.json alone (no gates, hours from size). 4. `applyState(ticket, state)` per §3.3: only an open ticket,
    only when newer, never undoes a merge, copies the PR url and alarm. 5. `buildRuns(docs, extra)` per §3.2: one
    run per name, else instance, else folder; the newer copy wins; status.json joins its run; ticket states attach by
    folder then by id; repo from the first PR url; returns `{runs, skipped, overlaid, states}`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json`, when buildRuns runs, then one run named view with 16 tickets results and every ticket field of SPEC §4.2 is filled as in `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/view.run.json`.

Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json` and `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/tickets/WV-11/state.json` (state coding, newer), when buildRuns runs, then WV-11 has status coding, stateNote set, and overlaid is 1.

Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/runs/view/beam.json` and `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/runs/edit/beam.json` plus an older copy of the view beam, when buildRuns runs, then two runs result, sorted by name, and the newer view copy is kept.
Given only `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/status.sample.json`, when buildRuns runs, then one run of kind status results with no gates and hours taken from size (S=4, M=7, L=11, XL=16).

Given a JSON file with neither tickets nor done/working/left nor id+state, when buildRuns runs, then it is counted in skipped and creates no run; a merged ticket with a newer state.json saying coding stays merged.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then parse.test.mjs passes against every fixture under `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/`.

tickets.summary: Open files and folders, drag and drop, reload and auto-reload
tickets.why:
People open the viewer from disk and point it at a .warp folder that keeps changing while the run goes.
    If reading a folder pulls in the whole repo, if dropping a folder does nothing, or if reload makes them pick the
    files again every time, they stop using it. The loader has to find the right files, remember how to re-read
    them, and keep working in browsers without the File System Access API.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/load/sources/sources.mjs` per SPEC §3.4. 1. `openFiles()` and `openFolder()` using
    showOpenFilePicker / showDirectoryPicker when present, else the hidden inputs (multiple, webkitdirectory).
    2. Folder walk: prefer a `.warp` child; read only files matching `(beam|status|state)*.json`; skip `.git`,
    `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `dist`, `build` and `previous-*`; depth 7. 3. Drop: file system handles when
    offered, else webkitGetAsEntry traversal. 4. `readSources(sources)` returns docs `{path, data, modified}`
    and errors per file. 5. `reload()`: re-read handles; a page with embedded data reloads the page; plain input
    files say to open again. 6. Auto-reload every 30 s when the tab is visible, remembered in localStorage inside
    try/catch. 7. `embeddedDocs(document)` reads the warp-data slot written by Warp's /warp-dashboard.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a fake directory handle holding `.warp/beam.json`, `.warp/tickets/WV-11/state.json`, `.warp/agents.json` and `node_modules/x/beam.json`, when the folder is read, then exactly the beam and the state file are returned with paths starting with the folder name.
Given the warp-data slot holds {files:[{path,data}]}, when embeddedDocs runs, then it returns those docs and reload() calls location.reload.
Given a browser without showOpenFilePicker, when Open status files is chosen, then the hidden file input is clicked and its files are read on change.
Given localStorage throws on access, when auto-reload is toggled, then no exception escapes and the toggle still works for the session.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then sources.test.mjs passes using fake handles and jsdom.

tickets.summary: Gate blocks: assign each ticket to a block and clear blocks
tickets.why:
Warp runs a plan in gate blocks and, by default, starts a block only when the blocks before it are
    cleared. The swimlane, the board lanes and the people-hour totals all depend on which block a ticket belongs to.
    If the viewer assigns blocks differently from Warp, the plan it draws is not the plan Warp runs and the gate
    lines land in the wrong place.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/model/blocks/blocks.mjs`, a port of Warp's scripts/blocks.py as specified in SPEC §6.
    1. `gateKeys(run)`: G-number keys in numeric order, then other keys in plan order. 2. `assignBlocks(run)`: a
    ticket's block is its own gate when that gate exists, else the lowest gate that lists it as a member, else the
    highest block among its dependencies (cycles cut), else the first block; with no gates every block is null.
    3. `blockStates(run)`: per block the ticket ids, counts of merged, open, parked and queued, the gate status and
    `cleared` (every ticket merged, done or skipped and the gate not red). 4. Sets `run.blockRank`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json`, when assignBlocks runs, then every ticket's block equals `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/view.blocks.json`.
Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/big/beam.sample.json` (68 tickets, gates G0–G5), when assignBlocks runs, then the result equals `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/big.blocks.json`.
Given a ticket with no gate, no membership and a dependency cycle A→B→A, when assignBlocks runs, then it terminates and both get the highest block of their other dependencies or the first block.
Given a run with no gates, when blockStates runs, then it returns an empty list and every ticket's block is null.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then blocks.test.mjs passes.

tickets.summary: Planned swimlane and actual timeline layouts
tickets.why:
The swimlane is the main screen: one row per agent slot on an estimate-hour clock, like the plan's swimlane
    PDF, and an actual clock of what happened. Both are computed, not drawn by hand. If the simulation differs from
    Warp's dispatch rule the picture lies about the finish and the critical chain; if the actual layout overlaps bars
    nobody can read it. This ticket owns both layouts as pure functions with golden outputs.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/model/plan/plan.mjs` per SPEC §7 and §8. 1. `plan(run)`: list scheduling with
    `run.cap` slots (maxAgents, default 18); a ticket is ready when every in-run dependency has merged (merge = end
    plus 0.5 h when its size is not auto-merged) and, with gateOrder strict, every earlier block has merged; ready
    tickets sorted critical first, starred, rank, longest downstream chain, natural id; lowest free slot. Sets
    `slot start end mergeAt` per ticket and `finish peak slots waves critHours critCount gateAt` on the run; tickets
    that can never be ready are laid after everything and flagged `unplaced`. 2. `layoutPlan(run)` and
    `layoutActual(run, now)` returning `{prefix, label, rows, span, now, unstarted, items, gates}` (§8): actual
    bars run from claimedAt (else PR opened, else first event) to mergedAt (else now) and pack into the lowest free row.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json`, when plan runs, then slot, start and mergeAt of every ticket and finish, peak, slots and gateAt equal `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/view.plan.json` to 0.01 h.
Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/big/beam.sample.json`, when plan runs, then the result equals `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/big.plan.json` (finish T+177, peak 10, 10 slots).
Given gateOrder deps on the same big beam, when plan runs, then no block waits for an earlier block and the finish is earlier than the strict finish.

Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json` and now = 2026-10-12T20:00:00Z, when layoutActual runs, then items, rows, unstarted and the now line equal `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/view.actual.json`.
Given a dependency cycle, when plan runs, then it returns within 100 ms, every ticket has a slot and the cycle members are flagged unplaced.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then plan.test.mjs passes.

tickets.summary: Run totals: estimate, agent hours, people hours, tickets
tickets.why:
The header answers how big the run is and how far it has got: the run estimate, agent hours, people
    hours and tickets, each split into completed, in progress, errored or parked, and to do. People use these numbers
    to decide whether to add agents or chase reviews, so they must follow Warp's own estimate rules and show a dash
    when the files do not carry a value, never an invented number.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/model/metrics/metrics.mjs` per SPEC §9. 1. `computeMetrics(runs)` returning the four
    totals and their bucket splits: agent hours from ticket hours (S=4, M=7, L=11, XL=16 unless the ticket has hours);
    people hours 0.5 h per ticket whose size is not auto-merged plus 0.5 h per blocking gate, a gate counted done when
    green, err when red, in progress when its block has started; run estimate = program.estimate.elapsedHours split by
    agent-hour share; tickets by bucket. 2. Elapsed hours since runStartedAt, ETA left (beam metrics.etaHours, else
    max(critical hours left, remaining hours / min(cap, 8))), swimlane finish, assumptions, actual hours, tokens,
    cost. 3. `utilization(runs)`: active (claimed through merging) over summed cap, hours spent over estimate.agentHours,
    tokens and minutes by size and by agent. Missing values are null.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json`, when computeMetrics runs, then every number equals `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/view.metrics.json`.

tickets.summary: Swimlane view: slots, time axis, gates, bars, zoom, actual clock
tickets.why:
This is the screen people open the viewer for: the run as a swimlane of agent slots like the plan's PDF,
    colored by each ticket's status now, with gate lines and the critical chain. It must stay readable from 16 to
    400 tickets, at any zoom, on a phone and on paper, and switch to the actual clock without changing what a color
    means. Without it the viewer is a list.
tickets.what:
Create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/view/swimlane/swimlane.mjs` and `swimlane.css` per SPEC §10.6. 1. `renderSwimlane(run,
    layout, opts)` returns HTML: sticky slot labels, a gate row with labels left of each line (labels that collide
    lift to a second row; names only when there is room; gates reached together share 'G2 · G8'), an axis row
    (T+ or + labels at steps 1,2,5,10,20,25,50,100,200 so ticks are at least 56 px apart), grid lines, gate lines
    (red bold when red, green when green), the now line on the actual clock, and one bar per item: left accent and
    tint in the status color, id with ★ for critical, size·hours, title, ⚠ for an alarm, ✗ for red CI, a tiny form
    under 70 px, dim when filtered out, outline when a search hits. 2. Zoom: fit to width times 6^(zoom/100);
    print width fit. 3. The Plan/Actual toggle in the panel header. 4. `tooltipFor(ticket)`.

Given a bar narrower than 70 px, when rendered, then only the id shows; given a search that matches it, then it gets the hit outline and every non-matching bar is dimmed.

    the legend, totals, swimlane, board and table must agree on every count. This ticket also fixes the extension
    points WarpEdit builds on, so the editor can add controls without touching viewer code, and proves the viewer
    itself has no control that changes a status.
tickets.what:
Complete `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/main.mjs` and create `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/src/store/store.mjs` per SPEC §11. 1. Store: docs, runs,
    tab, view, groupBy, colorBy, zoom, clock, sort, off categories, query, closed lanes; `subscribe(fn)`,
    `replaceRuns(runs, reason)` and `recompute(run)` (blocks + plan again after a status change). 2. Render loop:
    meta, headline, tabs, cards, utilization, legend, then the active view; one delegated click/keydown/dblclick
    handler; drawer open/close; toasts; drop overlay; reload; auto-reload. 3. Print: beforeprint fits the swimlane to
    1020 px and opens utilization, afterprint restores. 4. `createApp({root, plugins})` with hooks `drawerSections`,
    `headerActions`, `swimlaneOverlays`, `keys`; the viewer passes no plugins. 5. `app.test.mjs`: jsdom on the built
    page with each fixture.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app run release`, when run, then `WARPDEMO/WarpView/viewer.html` is written, is under 400 kB and opens from disk with the empty state.
Given viewer.html with `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/beam.sample.json` dropped on it, when compared, then blocks, plan, metrics and table order equal `WARPDEMO/WarpView/fixtures/expected/`.
Given viewer.html, when searched, then it has no element with data-edit, no 'Reset' control and no network URL in markup or script.
Given the README, when read, then it names WarpEdit for resets and gives the sample path fixtures/beam.sample.json.
Given `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`, when run, then parity.test.mjs passes.

nfrs.text: No network calls: the built file loads nothing from outside itself.

technicalDetails.apiContract: none (static page; module exports listed in SPEC §11)
technicalDetails.idempotency: Rendering is a pure function of the loaded files and the view state; loading the same files twice gives the same screen.
technicalDetails.implementerNotes: Repo layout: `WARPDEMO/WarpView/spec|plan|tickets|fixtures|ui` is the read-only pack; write code only under the lock folders above (inside `WARPDEMO/WarpView/app/`). Start with `Implement WV-16`. Run `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app ci` once, then `npm --prefix WARPDEMO/WarpView/app test`.
